transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 09:32 UTC
Duration: 68 minutes
Attendees: Ari Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), James Miller (Aurelius CTO), Priya Nair (Platform Eng), Carlos Ruiz (Security), Lina Gomez (SRE)

Auto-generated Summary (auto):
- Deep dive on Private VPC deployment: PrivateLink, NAT, subnets, DNS for runtime connectivity.
- Discussed runtime performance tradeoffs: batching, KV cache, quantization, network egress/latency impacts.
- Agreed next steps: share PrivateLink docs, provide CIDR ranges, schedule benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ari (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanna go deep on the private VPC setup and how that interacts with runtime performance, so Samira will walk through the architecture and then we'll take questions about batching, KV cache, quant, etc.
[00:12] James (Aurelius): Sounds good. We're mostly concerned about latency and data egress, and how PrivateLink impacts throughput. Also security folks will ask about audit logs and KMS.
[00:20] Samira (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda: 1) PrivateLink and connectivity options (PrivateLink vs VPC peering vs transit), 2) NAT and outbound internet needs for model updates, 3) subnet sizing and IPs for GPU nodes, 4) runtime considerations: KV cache, batching, quantization effects on network, 5) perf benchmarks.
[00:38] Priya (Aurelius): Quick context: our cluster is in us-east-1, 3 AZs. We want no public IPs on inference nodes, and strict egress control. We also use SAML SSO and a centralized KMS.
[00:50] Samira: That's common. PrivateLink is usually the best fit for "no public IP" nodes because it gives you an interface VPC endpoint to the Redwood control plane and the model artifact store. That eliminates need for IGW on the inference subnets.
[01:05] Carlos (Security): Can you be explicit on what traffic still needs egress to internet? For example OS updates, model downloads from third-party model hubs, telemetry?
[01:12] Samira: Sure. In short: with PrivateLink you can keep control plane and model pull over the endpoint. But for OS package updates you still either allow a restricted NAT with proxy or provide a local package mirror. Telemetry and metrics can be routed to our observability endpoint over PrivateLink if you opt in; otherwise you'll need outbound.
[01:30] Lina (SRE): If we use PrivateLink, how does DNS resolution work? We have private hosted zones in Route53 and some split-horizon DNS.
[01:38] Samira: We recommend using the VPC endpoint's private DNS name which rewrites the public FQDN to the VPC endpoint IP. You may need to ensure the Route53 resolver rules don't shadow those names; we provide a list of service FQDNs to whitelist.
[01:51] Ari: Also note that very large batch/streaming traffic can saturate the interface endpoints; they scale but you should size your ENIs and choose multiple subnets across AZs.
[02:04] James: Let's pivot to runtime performance. We plan to run local GPUs with your runtime. How does batching and KV cache affect latency under PrivateLink?
[02:12] Samira: Good question. Batching is internal to the serving layer and doesn't necessarily require additional network hops between customer app and the runtime — except for initial request/response payloads. KV cache is in-memory on the GPU hosts; if you have multi-host KV cache sharding there can be inter-host traffic. Our default in-VM KV cache avoids cross-host fetches for most warm sessions, but cold-starts may hit persistent storage over the endpoint for model weights or KV persist.
[02:37] Priya: When you say "KV cache sharding" does that mean if we scale horizontally we could get cross-host KV fetches that increase latency?
[02:44] Samira: Potentially yes, if the session is being served by a host that doesn't have the prefix cached. We mitigate with affinity routing (sticky sessions) and prefix-aware routing. For high throughput, we suggest larger warmup windows and preloading warm prompts.
[02:57] James: What about quantization — 4-bit/8-bit — any impact on network or latency?
[03:02] Samira: Quantization mainly reduces GPU memory and compute latency; network impact is minimal except when transferring model files for startup — quantized artifacts are smaller so pull is faster. One caveat: some kernels for lower-bit quant require different exec paths which can affect per-token latency by a few ms depending on sequence length. We'll share benchmark numbers.
[03:20] Ari: We'll also share a matrix of expected throughput per GPU type and quant level. For example, an A100 80GB at 4-bit with our optimizations reaches X tokens/sec (we'll provide actual numbers in the doc).
[03:33] Carlos: About audit logs and KMS: we need to ensure no plaintext model data leaves our VPC and that S3/obj store uses our KMS keys. Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS?
[03:41] Samira: Yes. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM for model artifact encryption and TLS certs; audit logs can be exported to your logging endpoints over PrivateLink or to an S3 bucket accessible in your account. We capture per-request metadata, but note that logs for low-level GPU ops are aggregated.
[03:58] James: Networking specifics: NATs vs no-NAT. Is NAT required for model downloads/upgrades?
[04:04] Samira: Not strictly. If you have PrivateLink and the model registry is exposed via the endpoint, you don't need NAT. But many customers prefer a managed NAT for external package repos. If you want zero egress, we can ship a bootstrap bundle of required packages and models into your object storage via an onboarding bucket.
[04:21] Lina: Subnet sizing — how many IPs per node? GPUs require one primary IP per host plus ENIs for endpoint traffic?
[04:29] Samira: Typically one ENI per host plus additional ENIs for throughput scaling. Reserve /24s per AZ for clusters of tens of hosts; for larger clusters we advise /22. We'll send a subnet sizing guide.
[04:40] Priya: Does Redwood require any special routing for traffic between infra and the serving nodes? We use managed CNI with AWS.
[04:45] Samira: No special routing beyond standard route table entries to the VPC endpoints and NAT. For multi-AZ latency, ensure placement groups or close AZ placement for GPU nodes if you want lowest inter-host latency.
[04:58] James: On benchmarking: can we run a test that measures p99 latency for 32-token generations at targeted QPS?
[05:03] Samira: Yes. Typical runbook: we provision identical workloads across shaded concurrency levels (1, 4, 8, 16), warm KV cache with a workload of similar prompt distributions, then measure p50/p95/p99 under steady state. We also test cold-start scenarios. We'll provide the runbook and a script.
[05:18] Ari: One more networking nuance — PrivateLink pricing and ENI limits. There are per-endpoint hourly charges and bandwidth considerations. If you want to avoid per-request egress billed per GB, we can architect an intra-region peering for high-volume traffic but that opens different security considerations.
[05:34] Carlos: Any compliance controls for PrivateLink? e.g., can we restrict which subnets endpoints attach to, and do you provide VPC flow logs?
[05:41] Samira: Yes, customers control endpoint subnets. We can push flow logs and VPC logs to your log destination. For SOC2/ISO we provide audit artifacts and can support periodic pen tests under NDA.
[05:55] Priya: What about rolling updates of models — will we ever call home from inside the private VPC to elect rollout policies?
[06:02] Samira: Model rollouts are controlled via the control plane. For Private deployments, you can run the control plane in your VPC or use our managed control plane over PrivateLink with a canary rollout config. Updates are pulled by the inference nodes; you can gate deployments and require manual approve.
[06:18] James: Are there known gotchas with split-horizon DNS and PrivateLink interfering with our internal services?
[06:25] Samira: Sometimes internal hostnames collide; we recommend dedicated private hosted zone prefixes for Redwood endpoints or using endpoint-specific hostnames we provide. Also check resolver rules precedence.
[06:33] Lina: About failover — if an AZ goes down and PrivateLink endpoints are in that AZ, how does traffic reroute?
[06:40] Samira: Endpoints are regional; the interface ENIs are per-AZ. If an AZ loses connectivity, traffic will route to endpoints in other AZs but you must have ENIs in multiple AZs and route tables to support cross-AZ traffic. We recommend multi-AZ endpoints for HA.
[06:56] Priya: Let's talk numbers — what impact on per-request latency should we expect from PrivateLink vs public egress?
[07:03] Samira: PrivateLink often reduces variance and avoids IGW hop, so p99 is usually better or comparable; raw median latency might be a few ms different depending on path. The dominant latency is local model decoding per token, not the network hop for most workloads. Network affects cold-starts and cross-host KV fetches more.
[07:20] James: For our HIPAA workload, data residency and audit trail is critical. Can the logs be stored in our account?
[07:26] Ari: Yes, for Private deployments we can push logs to your S3 and KMS. We'll document the retention and fields.
[07:34] Samira: Also note data-at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys is supported.
[07:38] James: Cool. Any advice on batching config for low-latency chat UX?
[07:42] Samira: For chat, use small dynamic batching with max latency threshold (e.g., 8-12ms) and token-based batching rather than request-count batching. Streaming reduces perceived latency. We can tune the threshold based on your target p50/p95.
[07:55] Priya: For KV cache, how do you persist the cache across node restarts?
[07:59] Samira: We persist minimal metadata and use fast local NVMe for snapshotting; on restart we rehydrate from persisted objects in your S3 over PrivateLink. That can add ~100-400ms for a warmup depending on prefix size.
[08:12] James: Any concerns about TCP connections and long-lived streams over PrivateLink?
[08:17] Samira: Keep-alive is fine; we recommend configuring idle timeouts greater than your expected stream length. LB idle timeouts in some setups can cut streams; we provide recommended ALB/NLB config.
[08:30] Ari: Ok we are at ~36 minutes in the call; let's do quick recap and next steps.
[08:36] Ari: Recap: Redwood to share PrivateLink setup guide, subnet sizing guide, benchmark runbook, and quant/perf matrix. Aurelius to share CIDRs and SAML/KMS details. Pilot SOW and pricing by Ari.
[08:49] James: That works. Also can you include a sample CloudFormation and a Terraform snippet?
[08:53] Samira: Yes we'll include both.
[08:56] Lina: One last Q — will the rollout require extra NAT throughput for model pushes?
[09:00] Samira: If you avoid NAT by using PrivateLink for the artifact store, pushes can be internal. If you need external downloads then plan NAT bandwidth accordingly.
[09:07] Ari: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by end of week.

End of transcript.
